newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore hotels to post sluggish 1996 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Singapore hotels to post sluggish 1996 earnings.

text.p: Singapore hotels are likely to post flat to lower earnings for 1996 due to a sharp slowdown in visitor arrivals, excess room supply and a strong domestic currency, analysts said at the weekend.
They said the hotel industry's outlook remained bleak over the next few years despite a projected slowdown in room supply growth as tourist arrivals were not expected to pick up significantly.
Only hotel groups with significant interests in property development like Orchard Parade Holdings Ltd and Marco Polo Developments Ltd were seen posting better than average 1996 earnings.
Most of Singapore's listed hotel groups are expected to report their full-year results over the next month.
"For the past year, domestic earnings for hotels will definitely shrink...It's basically an industry that will be in the doldrums for a while," said Pearly Yap, an analyst with Crosby Securities.
She said hotel occupancy rates were likely to come under pressure as room rates were among the cheapest in the region.

According to the consensus forecast in the latest Estimate Directory, Republic Hotels & Resorts is expected to post net earnings of Singapore $25.8 million (US$18.2 million) for 1996, against S$23.4 million in 1995.
Orchard Parade is seen posting net profit of S$38.7 million against S$11.8 million in 1995.
However, Overseas Union Enterprise Ltd was expected to post a slight increase in net profit of S$38.3 million for 1996, against 1995's S$37.5 million.
"I don't think there'll be any surprises in the final year results. Everybody's going to expect consolidation for the next two or three years," said an analyst with another brokerage.

He said hotel groups were likely to see more of their earnings growth coming from their investment holdings and property income as occupancy and room rates came under pressure from increased room supply.

The supply of hotel rooms grew more than nine percent last year, with the opening of the 612-room Ritz-Carlton, the 509-room Conrad International and the 338-room Grand Plaza, Vickers Ballas said in a recent research report.

Vickers Ballas analyst Leong Chi Meng said the rate of room supply growth was expected to slow to 3.7 percent this year but occupancy levels could still fall below 80 percent due to the gap between room growth and tourist arrivals.
Growth in arrivals fell to 2.2 percent last year, marking the fifth year of declining growth and the lowest level seen since 1991, according to the Singapore Tourist Promotion Board (STPB).
The STPB attributed the weak growth mainly to a drop in arrivals from Japan, the city-state's top visitor-generating market, for the first time in five years.
More regional travellers also opted to visit Hong Kong instead of Singapore ahead of the territory's handover to China in July this year, the STPB said.
"The pressure is of course on the upmarket hotels but that's flowed through to the three- and four-star hotels as well," said Crosby's Yap.
As a result, she said, the earnings of even Republic Hotels & Resorts, with its focus on the traditionally popular three- and four-star hotel segment, would be adversely affected.
Yap said Republic Hotels was likely to post a five percent increase in 1996 earnings, against her previous projection of 12 percent growth.
But she said the hotel's stock remained attractive because it was a well run company, with a niche market and a strong appetite for acquisitions.

Leong of Vickers was more bullish on Republic's earnings outlook, saying the group was likely to post 8.5 percent growth in 1996 and 39 percent this year due to improved contributions from its Novotel Orchid and Orchard hotels in Singapore and its its hotel in Indonesia.
